csv-report.prompt: Build a command-line tool report.py (Python 3, standard library only) that summarises sales records. Usage: `python3 report.py FILE [FILE ...]`. Each FILE is CSV with the header row `date,region,product,units,unit_price`; units is a non-negative integer and unit_price a non-negative decimal. Print one JSON object to stdout: {"rows": the number of valid rows, "revenue": the sum of units * unit_price rounded to 2 decimals, "by_region": revenue per region rounded to 2 decimals, "by_product": total units per product}. A row with the wrong number of columns, or a non-numeric or negative units or unit_price, is skipped and reported on stderr as `FILE:LINE: <reason>` (the header is line 1), and the exit code is then 2; otherwise it is 0. A file that cannot be read prints an error on stderr without a traceback, prints nothing on stdout and exits 1. A file with only a header contributes nothing. Cover the behaviour with unittest tests that run with `python3 -m unittest`.

checkers.prompt: Build a small two-player Checkers game served by a Node.js HTTP server with no npm dependencies. server.js starts the server on the port in the PORT environment variable (default 3000). GET / serves a playable HTML page titled "Checkers" with an 8x8 board where two players take turns on the same page. GET /api/new starts a game and returns JSON with a game id. Red starts on rows 0 to 2 and moves first toward higher row numbers; black starts on rows 5 to 7; pieces sit on the squares where row plus column is odd. POST /api/move with JSON {"game": id, "from": [row, col], "to": [row, col]} returns JSON with "ok" true or false, "turn" set to "red" or "black", and "winner" null or the winning colour. An illegal move returns "ok": false and leaves the turn unchanged; a legal move switches the turn; a jump removes the jumped piece and is mandatory when available; a piece reaching the far row becomes a king. Keep the game rules in a module the server uses, and cover them with node:test tests under test/ that run with `node --test`.
checks: log=$(mktemp); node --test > "$log" 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -Eq '^(ℹ|#) pass [1-9]' "$log" && [ $rc -eq 0 ]; r=$?; rm -f "$log"; exit $r

python3 "$E2E_CHECKS/serve.py" -- node -e "const base=process.env.BASE; const post=(b)=>fetch(base+'/api/move',{method:'POST',headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(b)}).then(r=>r.json()); (async()=>{const g=await fetch(base+'/api/new').then(r=>r.json()); const id=g.game??g.id??g.gameId; if(id===undefined) process.exit(2); const bad=await post({game:id,from:[2,1],to:[2,2]}); if(bad.ok!==false||bad.turn!=='red') process.exit(3); const good=await post({game:id,from:[2,1],to:[3,2]}); if(good.ok!==true||good.turn!=='black') process.exit(4); process.exit(0);})().catch(()=>process.exit(6))"

chess-salesforce.prompt: Build a chess rules engine in Apex with a simple Lightning web component board, in a Salesforce DX project in the current directory, and deploy and test it in the Salesforce Developer Edition org with alias `de`. Use `--target-org de` on every `sf` command that talks to the org; the CLI is already logged in, so never ask for, print or store credentials, and never run `sf org display` (it prints an access token). Name every Apex class `SLChess...` (for example `SLChessEngine`) and the component `slChessBoard`. Besides the Apex classes and the component, create exactly these kinds of metadata, all named with the prefix `SLChess`, so that the board opens in the org and the work can still be removed afterwards: a custom tab `tabs/SLChess_Board.tab-meta.xml` that is a Lightning component tab (`<lwcComponent>slChessBoard</lwcComponent>`; the component's meta file exposes the `lightning__Tab` target), a Lightning app `applications/SLChess.app-meta.xml` (standard navigation, containing that tab) and, if you want one, a Lightning app page `flexipages/SLChess_<Name>.flexipage-meta.xml` (then the component's meta file also exposes `lightning__AppPage`). Create no other metadata (no custom objects, fields, permission sets, static resources, triggers, profiles, labels or flows), and do not change profiles or permission sets. The Salesforce DX project root (`sfdx-project.json` and `force-app/`) is the current directory itself, not a subfolder. `SLChessEngine` is a public class with static methods only; a position is a FEN string. `startFen()` returns the standard start position. `legalMoves(String fen)` returns a `List<String>` of every legal move for the side to move in UCI form (for example `e2e4`, and `e7e8q` for a promotion), sorted alphabetically. `applyMove(String fen, String move)` returns the FEN after the move, with correct castling rights, en-passant square, halfmove clock and fullmove number, or throws `SLChessEngine.IllegalMoveException` (a public exception class you define inside `SLChessEngine`) when the move is not legal. The en-passant target square is set after every two-square pawn push, whether or not a capture is possible (the FEN-spec convention). `status(String fen)` returns `ongoing`, `check`, `checkmate` or `stalemate` for the side to move. Implement all piece moves, castling on both sides (never out of, through or into check; in UCI it is the king's two-square move: `e1g1`, `e1c1`, `e8g8`, `e8c8`), en passant, promotion to q, r, b or n, check, checkmate and stalemate. The component `slChessBoard` renders a FEN as an 8x8 board and is a game two people can play by turns on one screen: a person picks a piece and then a destination, the board shows whose turn it is and the game status (check, checkmate, stalemate), refuses an illegal destination, lets a pawn promote (queen is acceptable as the default) and has a New game button. It calls `SLChessController` and renders what comes back. `SLChessController` has `@AuraEnabled public static` methods `legalMoves(String fen)`, returning a `List<String>`, `applyMove(String fen, String move)`, returning the new FEN as a `String`, and `status(String fen)`, returning `ongoing`, `check`, `checkmate` or `stalemate` as a `String`, so that the grader can call them. The grader calls `SLChessController` only with legal moves and calls `SLChessEngine.applyMove` directly for an illegal one, so the controller may report an illegal move however suits the board (for example by throwing an `AuraHandledException`). The work will be graded by playing complete games, ply by ply, through `SLChessController` (`legalMoves`, `applyMove` and `status`), each game in one anonymous Apex run. Cover the rules with Apex tests in classes named `SLChess...Test` that run in the org, at least 8 Apex test methods in all: include known games (fool's mate, scholar's mate), castling, en passant, promotion, stalemate and move counts from standard test positions. Deploy with `sf project deploy start --target-org de` and run the tests in the org, one test class at a time, with `sf apex run test --target-org de --class-names <TestClass> --synchronous --result-format human --code-coverage` (a synchronous run takes one class). Keep the engine efficient enough that `legalMoves` on a middlegame position finishes well inside the synchronous Apex CPU limit, and so that a whole depth-2 legal-move enumeration (every legal reply to every legal move of a position, counted) runs inside one transaction, and so that a whole game of about 35 plies played through `SLChessController` (`legalMoves`, `applyMove` and `status` for every ply) does too. Do not stop until the tests pass in the org.

battleship-salesforce.prompt: Build a single-player Battleship game in Apex with a simple Lightning web component board, in a Salesforce DX project in the current directory, and deploy and test it in the Salesforce Developer Edition org with alias `de`. Use `--target-org de` on every `sf` command that talks to the org; the CLI is already logged in, so never ask for, print or store credentials, and never run `sf org display` (it prints an access token). Name every Apex class `SLBattle...` (for example `SLBattleEngine`) and the component `slBattleBoard`. Besides the Apex classes and the component, create exactly these kinds of metadata, all named with the prefix `SLBattle`, so that the board opens in the org for the user the CLI is logged in as and the work can still be removed afterwards: a custom tab `tabs/SLBattle_Board.tab-meta.xml` that is a Lightning component tab (`<lwcComponent>slBattleBoard</lwcComponent>`; the component's meta file exposes the `lightning__Tab` target), a Lightning app `applications/SLBattle.app-meta.xml` (standard navigation, containing that tab) and a permission set `permissionsets/SLBattle_Access.permissionset-meta.xml` that grants the app (`<applicationVisibilities>` with `<visible>true</visible>`), the tab (`<tabSettings>` with `<visibility>Visible</visibility>`) and the `SLBattleEngine` and `SLBattleController` classes (`<classAccesses>` with `<enabled>true</enabled>`). A new tab is hidden from every user until a permission set or profile grants it, so after you deploy, assign the permission set to the logged-in user with `sf org assign permset --name SLBattle_Access --target-org de`. Create no other metadata (no custom objects, fields, other permission sets, static resources, triggers, profiles, labels, flows or app pages), and do not change profiles or any other permission set. The Salesforce DX project root (`sfdx-project.json` and `force-app/`) is the current directory itself, not a subfolder. The game: the computer places a fleet on a 10x10 grid (rows and columns 0 to 9) and the player fires at it. The fleet is the standard one: `carrier` (5 cells), `battleship` (4), `cruiser` (3), `submarine` (3) and `destroyer` (2); every ship lies straight along one row or one column, entirely inside the grid, and no two ships share a cell. A ship is sunk when all of its cells have been hit, and the game is over when the last ship is sunk. `SLBattleEngine` is a public class with static methods only; a game is a JSON string. `newGame(Integer seed)` returns a new game whose fleet is placed at random from the seed: the same seed always gives the same fleet, in any transaction and however many games came before, and two different seeds give different fleets (Apex has no seeded random number generator, so write a small one). `fire(String game, Integer row, Integer col)` returns the game after one shot at that cell. The game JSON is an object with at least these keys: `shots` (the number of shots fired so far), `shipsLeft` (the number of ships not yet sunk), `gameOver` (`false` until the shot that sinks the last ship, `true` from that shot on) and `lastShot`, which is `null` in a new game and after a shot is an object `{"row": r, "col": c, "result": "miss" | "hit" | "sunk", "ship": name, "size": cells}`: `result` is `sunk` (not `hit`) for the shot that sinks a ship, and `ship` and `size` give that ship's name and number of cells on that shot only (they are `null` on a miss or a hit). Where the ships are and which cells were fired at is up to you; the board must not show a ship cell before it is hit. A shot at a cell that was already fired at, or with a row or a column outside 0 to 9, throws `SLBattleEngine.InvalidShotException` (a public exception class you define inside `SLBattleEngine`). After the game is over, a shot at a cell not yet fired at is still accepted: it is a `miss` and `gameOver` stays `true`. `SLBattleController` has `@AuraEnabled public static` methods `newGame(Integer seed)` and `fire(String game, Integer row, Integer col)`, each returning the game JSON as a `String`, so that the board and the grader can call them. The grader calls `SLBattleController` only with valid shots and calls `SLBattleEngine.fire` directly for an invalid one, so the controller may report an invalid shot however suits the board (for example by throwing an `AuraHandledException`). The component `slBattleBoard` renders the 10x10 grid, fires at a cell when a person clicks it, shows hits, misses and sunk ships, the number of shots fired and of ships left, says when the game is over and has a New game button. It calls `SLBattleController` and renders what comes back. The work will be graded by playing whole games through `SLBattleController`: `newGame` with a seed, then `fire` once at each of the 100 cells, each game in one anonymous Apex run. Cover the rules with Apex tests in classes named `SLBattle...Test` that run in the org, at least 8 Apex test methods in all: include the fleet (names, sizes, straight, inside the grid, no shared cell, the same seed twice), a miss, a hit, a sink, game over, a shot after game over and both kinds of invalid shot. Deploy with `sf project deploy start --target-org de` and run the tests in the org, one test class at a time, with `sf apex run test --target-org de --class-names <TestClass> --synchronous --result-format human --code-coverage` (a synchronous run takes one class). Keep the engine efficient enough that a whole game of 100 shots played through `SLBattleController` (`newGame`, then `fire` at every cell) runs inside one transaction. Do not stop until the tests pass in the org.

user-listing.prompt: This directory is an existing Node.js project with no npm dependencies (README.md describes it): an in-memory user store and its HTTP server, src/server.js, which `npm start` runs on the port in the PORT environment variable. Extend the server's user listing, GET /users, with filtering and pagination. The `name` query parameter keeps only the users whose name contains it as plain text, ignoring case; an empty `name` keeps every user. The `page` and `size` query parameters ask for one page of those users in id order, page 1 holding the first `size` of them. When either is given, the answer is a JSON object with "page", "size", "total" (how many users matched), "pages" (how many pages they fill, 0 when none matched) and "items" (the users on that page); `size` is 10 when only `page` is given and `page` is 1 when only `size` is given, and a page after the last one answers an empty "items". `page` must be a whole number of at least 1 and `size` a whole number from 1 to 100: any other value, an empty one included, answers HTTP 400 with a JSON object whose "error" says what is wrong. Keep the API compatible: without `page` and `size`, GET /users still answers a JSON array of users in id order (every user unless `name` is given), any other query parameter is ignored, and GET /users/:id is unchanged. Everything the project already does keeps working, and its existing tests must still pass as they are. Add node:test tests under test/ for the new behaviour; `npm test` runs them with the existing ones.

ticket-escalation.prompt: Extend the ticket service with bulk reassignment and escalation. `POST /tickets/reassign` with `{"from": "<agent>", "to": "<agent>"}` moves every open or in-progress ticket assigned to `from` over to `to` and answers `{"moved": <how many>, "ids": [<their ids in id order>]}`; `from` and `to` must be two different agents. Urgent tickets must not wait unassigned: when an open, unassigned, urgent ticket is older than ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES minutes (an environment variable, default 60), the agent named in the ONCALL environment variable is notified that the ticket was escalated; without ONCALL nothing is escalated. A ticket is escalated at most once, even across restarts of the service. Everything the service already does keeps working, assignment included, and the existing tests must still pass. count() { (cd "$1" && node --test 2>&1) | sed -nE 's/^(ℹ|#) pass ([0-9]+).*/\2/p' | tail -1; }; before=$(count "$PRIOR_WORK"); after=$(count .); echo "tests $before -> $after"; [ -n "$after" ] && [ "${after:-0}" -ge "${before:-0}" ] || { echo "fewer tests pass than in the followed run"; exit 1; }; added=$(diff -rN "$PRIOR_WORK/test" test 2>/dev/null | grep "^>"); [ -n "$added" ] || { echo "the test files are unchanged since the followed run"; exit 1; }; for word in reassign escalat; do printf "%s\n" "$added" | grep -qi "$word" || { echo "no added test line names $word"; exit 1; }; done; echo "no fewer tests pass, and the added test lines name reassignment and escalation"

ids() { grep -oE '\bR-[0-9]+\b' "$1/docs/shiploop/spec.md" 2>/dev/null | sort -u; }; before=$(mktemp); after=$(mktemp); ids "$PRIOR_WORK" > "$before"; ids . > "$after"; missing=$(comm -23 "$before" "$after" | tr '\n' ' '); added=$(comm -13 "$before" "$after" | tr '\n' ' '); earlier=$(wc -l < "$before"); rm -f "$before" "$after"; covered=no; grep -qi escalat docs/shiploop/spec.md && ! grep -qi escalat "$PRIOR_WORK/docs/shiploop/spec.md" && covered=yes; echo "earlier ids: $earlier; missing: $missing; added: $added; feature in spec: $covered"; [ "$earlier" -gt 0 ] && [ -z "$missing" ] && { [ -n "$added" ] || [ "$covered" = yes ]; }
ticket-escalation.retention_source: SPEC S-11: knowledge from the followed run is retained in the repository and built on, as in battleship-scoring: every earlier file kept, no dependency added, no fewer tests passing, the test files changed and naming reassignment and escalation, and the living spec keeping every earlier requirement ID while it records escalation

Graded against the followed run's delivery: pass-to-pass checks reuse checks/ticket_assignment_accept.py and ask whether the second run kept what the first one built. CONTRIBUTING.md 'Background work runs in the worker ... WORKER_INTERVAL_MS=0 must stop all of it' and docs/decisions/0006-notification-outbox.md: with the worker off, reads and edits of an urgent, unassigned ticket escalate nothing, even with ONCALL set and ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES=0
the request: '`POST /tickets/reassign` ... moves every open or in-progress ticket assigned to `from` over to `to` and answers `{"moved": <how many>, "ids": [<their ids in id order>]}`'

the request: '`from` and `to` must be two different agents', with docs/decisions/0004-error-envelope.md for the refusal (400 invalid in the envelope) and the first request's agent: a non-empty name of at most 64 characters
the request: 'Each moved ticket's new agent is notified as for a single assignment', with docs/decisions/0006-notification-outbox.md: through the outbox, delivered once by the worker
CONTRIBUTING.md 'Changes go through the store' and docs/decisions/0007-append-only-audit-log.md: each moved ticket gains one audit entry with the X-Actor actor and the assignee before and after
the request: 'the agent named in the ONCALL environment variable is notified that the ticket was escalated; without ONCALL nothing is escalated', through the outbox (docs/decisions/0006)

the request: 'when an open, unassigned, urgent ticket is older than ESCALATE_AFTER_MINUTES minutes': assigned, high, in-progress and resolved tickets are not escalated, and with 1 minute a ticket under two seconds old is not either
the request: 'A ticket is escalated at most once, even across restarts of the service', read with docs/decisions/0008-json-data-file.md: a restart from DATA_FILE escalates it no second time
